why: Both moved the same traffic correctly — create_client's two SDK clients, the four inline reviewer clients, the ICLR benchmark, and (the big one) aider via LiteLLM — and both found the same blocking seed=0 trade-off and the pre-existing anthropic-1.13 temperature break, with honest accounting of the n>1 ensemble and the non-catalog model pins. B edges ahead on correctness and depth of the system read: a full 41-id catalog audit with prices, two distinct caching mechanisms (Claude prefix caching measured at -67% plus OpenAI prompt_cache_key) rather than one, a broader seed glob that also covers the batch path, corrected codemod defects (silently-no-op imports, three duplicate runtime copies), and an operational layer A lacks — per-deployment capped keys with the correct 'caps apply after usage is recorded, so parallel runs overshoot' semantics, structured output to replace the regex JSON scraper, and provider_timeout gated on widening the retry decorator first.
A_best: Two mutually exclusive, measured, decision-ready options for the hard-coded reviewer stage (same-family gpt-4o vs gpt-5.4-mini on Flex at 82% less per call), delivered as validated branches alongside four others — the clearest 'approve one of these' package of the two.
B_best: The system read is grounded in what this pipeline actually is — an unattended batch job where one exception discards hours of GPU work — and it follows that through to the right levers: resilience and spend blast-radius (capped per-deployment keys, overshoot under --parallel), two different cache mechanisms measured separately, Flex correctly identified as unreachable until the model pins move, and the honest note that porting the ensemble off n costs ~67% more and buys coverage, not savings.
A_worst: It declines both cross-vendor fallbacks and provider_timeout on provenance/abandonment grounds, which under-serves an unattended pipeline that loses whole runs to hangs and crashes (a same-family fallback or a timeout plus widened retry would have been the expert move), and its seed-drop glob is scoped to get_response_from_llm only, so the n=1 batch path from iclr_analysis keeps seed and stays on OpenAI for no reason.
B_worst: Most of the highest-leverage system changes — Flex, fallbacks, timeout, structured output, the ensemble port — are proposals contingent on a model-pin decision B declines to make, so fewer of its ideas arrive as shippable branches than A's; neither engineer reaches shadow models, Jev, or Switchyard, or questions whether some calls (e.g. the five-member reflect-on-your-own-review loop) should exist at all.
